questions.prompt: Which habits lower the risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes? Choose all that apply.
options: A balanced diet with plenty of vegetables
questions.explain: Healthy habits prevent many non-communicable diseases.

questions.prompt: The recommended physical activity for teenagers is at least 60 minutes a day. How many hours is that in a week?
In the Healthy Day Planner, a day with 6 hours of sleep and 5 hours of screen time scored low. Which change helps most?
options: More sleep and less screen time
questions.explain: Teenagers need 9–11 hours of sleep; screens before bed disturb sleep.

questions.prompt: Why is type 2 diabetes described as a lifestyle-related disease?
options: It is caused by a virus
Its risk is strongly linked to diet, activity and weight, as well as genes
questions.explain: Healthy habits greatly reduce the risk.

questions.prompt: Which is part of good mental health?
options: Talking to trusted people, rest, and time with friends and nature
questions.explain: Health includes mental and social wellbeing.

questions.prompt: India has a growing number of people with type 2 diabetes. Suggest three changes a school could make to help students build healthy habits, and justify each.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) A daily activity period or sports and yoga for all students, since regular activity keeps weight healthy and the body using sugar well. 2) Healthier canteens: millets, fruit, and fewer fried and sugary items, and water instead of cola, which lowers sugar and fat intake. 3) Lessons and campaigns on sleep, screen time and nutrition, involving parents, because habits formed young tend to last for life. These reduce the risk factors for type 2 diabetes.
rubric: Each justified with a risk factor
questions.explain: Criterion D: prevention in the community.

items.label: Using a phone in bed late at night
Five servings of fruit and vegetables
Two cans of cola a day

questions.text: Diseases that are not caused by germs and cannot spread from person to person are called ___ diseases.
questions.explain: Examples: diabetes, heart disease, some cancers.
